newsitem.title: BURKINA FASO: Court confirms election win for Burkina president's party.
newsitem.headline: Court confirms election win for Burkina president's party.

text.p: Burkina Faso's supreme court released final results of the May 11 parliamentary elections, giving President Blaise Compaore's party 97 of the 111 seats in the assembly.
Results were cancelled in two districts which provisional results showed were won by Compaore's Congress for Democracy and Progress (CDP).
The court on Saturday cited "numerous irregularities which cast doubt on the sincerity of the vote and affected the results".
Voting will be repeated for three seats in the Kourittenga district in the centre-east and one in Oudalan, in the north.
Compaore's allies in the Alliance for Democracy and Federation (ADF) of Minister of State for Integration and African Solidarity Herman Yameogo won two seats.
Joseph Ki-Zerbo's opposition Party for Democracy and Progress (PDP) won six seats, the African Democratic Rally (RDA) of former prime minister Gerard Kango Ouedraogo, won two.
Compaore's party held 88 out of 107 seats in the outgoing national assembly, which was elected in 1992.
Parliament amended the constitution in January to increase the size of the assembly to 111.
Cash-strapped opposition parties, while hoping for victory, had said they would be content with an increased stake in the new parliament.
Compaore came to power in a 1987 army coup in which populist leader Thomas Sankara, his former close friend, was killed.
The constitution initially limited him to one seven-year term. Parliament in January voted to let him stand as many times as he wants. The next presidential election is due in 1998.
Turnout was 44.53 percent, compared to 35 percent in 1992.
